column4: Creative Philippines (Malikhaing Pinoy) Program
column6:
The Philippines is well known as a highly creative nation leveraging its rich cultural and diverse community across the country. This banks on the world ­class talent and ingenuity of the Filipinos that are globally known throughout the years. 

Recognizing the immense potential of the sector with a minimum value added of 7.12% of the total, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) has identified the Creative Industries as a priority sector in its new STl-driven industrial policy that aims to develop globally competitive and innovative industries. In line with this, the Philippine Creative Industries Development Act (R.A. No. 11904) provides the necessary support to drive the development and promotion of the Philippine creative industries, by creating market opportunities, promoting employment generation, nurturing human resources, ensuring financial-enabling mechanisms, and providing incentives to encourage and sustain Filipino excellence in the creative industries. The law also includes the creation of the Philippine Creative Industries Development Council, of which the National Secretariat shall be established under the DTI. 

With this, the DTI Competitiveness and Innovation Group (DTI-CIG) has conducted industry studies, stakeholder consultations, focus group discussions, and workshops, covering the sectors of digital advertising, digital animation, film, game development, software development, toys and characters, and TV, radio, and print, to assess the state of the Philippine Creative Industries and formulate strategies to advance the creative economy. 

Based on these, cross-cutting issues and constraints hinder its development, such as the lack of official statistics, limited access to capital, skills mismatch, limited access to new technologies, and limited access to global value chains. 

To address these issues, the DTI-CIG proposes the Creative Philippines (Malikhaing Pinoy) Program, a holistic set of programs encompassing knowledge expansion, development, growth, and sustainability. These programs are: 

1. Creative Domain-Specific Industry Studies (To Address the Lack of Scoping and Information)
2. Creative Venture Fund (To Address the Limited Access to Capital)
3. Creative Learning Academy (To Address Skills Mismatch)
4. Creative Innovation Centers (To Address Limited Access to New Technologies)
5. Creative Market Acceleration Program (To Address Limited Access to Global Value Chain)

To ensure a sustainable foundation in the effective implementation of these programs, the DTI-CIG will also support the establishment of the National Secretariat which will implement the Creative Philippines Program, and the Creative Industries Development Plan, which will define the road to development. Furthermore, the DTI-CIG recognizes the necessity of initiatives for advocacy and awareness, as well as strong industry ­government academe collaboration. 

This comprehensive and holistic approach will significantly improve the Creative Industries' competitiveness, enhance stakeholders' capability, increase productivity, facilitate export promotion and development, and permit compliance with global standards for greater market access; thereby, positioning the country as an emerging creative hub in the global market.

column4: Development and Adoption of the Philippine Skills Framework (PSF) for Business Functions
column6:
The Philippine Skills Framework (PSF) is a reference or tool for industry stakeholders, including PTTC, to identify functional and enabling skills and competencies required in various job roles in the industry.  It contains skills documents - career map, skills map, and skills and competencies documents - containing information that are the building blocks for the creation of progressive job adverts, performance management system, certificate courses, and industry-ready degree programs. 

There are  8 priority industry sectors for PSF, 3 of which have been completed and launched in 2021-2022.  These include PSF for Digital Art and Animation, Game Development, and Supply Chains and Logistics.  Development of PSFs for remaining priority industries are in the pipeline already. 
The PTTC is mandated to deliver business management training services, or specifically provision of training and learning programs in  marketing, production, human resource, information management, financial management, and business management  to hone the skills of our budding and existing entrepreneurs serving both the domestic and export or international markets. As an innovation to the sector-specific PSFs, PTTC takes the initiative to develop PSF for these business functions, or are called cross-sectoral skills framework.

But by 2011, during the celebration of the Philippine Independence Day, the clock once again was restored to its former glory. A famous Korean car manufacturing firm sponsored the restoration project of the iconic Flower Clock.

column4: Year of Philippine Design
column6:
The Year of Philippine Design operationalizes the Philippines’ first National Design Policy with the ambition to unleash the transformative power of design in the Philippines, cultivating a future where Filipino innovations flourish, global impact is realized, social transformation is enabled, and future generations are empowered to create a brighter tomorrow. 
 
The National Design Policy serves as our blueprint for steering the Philippines toward a design-driven future. To achieve this vision, we have identified five (5) priority areas and outlined 10 strategic actions to be implemented over the next 5 years. These initiatives aim to embed design into our country’s socioeconomic transformation and establish a solid foundation for long-term impact: 
•	Increase Design Awareness: Create recognition and pride for Philippine design excellence 
•	Professionalize the Design Sector: Elevate global competitiveness and impact of Philippine design sectors 
•	Embed Design in Business: Embed design for business transformation and acceleration 
•	Infuse Design in Policy-Making: Infuse design thinking to modernize policy-making 
•	Enhance Design Skills: Develop design as a national skillset and mindset

column4: Development of Eco-Park, Operationalization and Enhancement of Tourism Hostel, Caramoan Campus

The project involves establishment of an Eco-Tourism Park that will support to the university's program on Eco-Tourism. The ecological park's primary goals are to teach visitors about local ecology and the need for environmental protection, as well as to provide public recreation while enhancing and protecting the site's natural environment. The Partido State University Caramoan Campus’ Eco-Park involves the development of approximately 300 square meters of area located in the vicinity of the campus. This project will benefit the flagship programs of Caramoan Campus: BS Eco-tourism, BS in Hotel and Restaurant Management and BS in Conservation Biology and Restoration Ecology.
The ParSU Caramoan Eco-Park seeks to develop an ecological park that will include a picnic area, leisure, and rest area, a view deck, and a botanical and butterfly garden with the use of indigenous materials.
The Operationalization of the Campus Hostel, on the other hand, is an income-generating project that has a great potential. In line with the campus’ goal to produce quality, morally and culturally upright graduates in sustainable Tourism and Hospitality Management, the campus will implement the transition of ParSU Caramoan Hostel to an Eco Hostel which will make operational and environmental improvements to lessen its negative impact on the environment. The Eco Hostel will not only be a training ground for BSHM and BSTM students but will also be a source of income for the campus while promoting environmental conservation and restoration. 
The improvement plans for the hostel includes the Conversion of the ParSU Caramoan Hostel to an Eco-hostel, installation of motion-sensing faucets, repainting of the hostel and Implementation of a waste management system.

column4: TRAVEL Project: Tourism Readiness and Advancement through Values, Education, and Local Empowerment
column6:
The project will involve a series of structured training sessions, hands-on
workshops, and community-based planning activities designed to build the capacity of local tourism stakeholders. The target participants include local tour guides, resort staff, small entrepreneurs, youth volunteers, cultural bearers, and representatives from people’s organizations and local government units involved in tourism. The core components of the activity are as follows:
 Activity 1: Training on Basic Hospitality and Tourist Handling. Participants
will undergo workshops on customer service, frontliner etiquette, basic communication
skills, and handling guests of different cultural backgrounds.
 Activity 2: Sustainable and Responsible Tourism Practices. Sessions will
focus on environmental awareness, cultural sensitivity, solid waste management, and
eco-tourism practices that protect local natural and heritage assets. 
3. Activity 3: Entrepreneurship and Local Product Development. Locals will be
taught how to package tourism-related products and services, set appropriate prices, and engage in small-scale tourism enterprises (e.g., homestays, guided tours, local
crafts, food offerings). 
4. Activity 4: Destination Mapping and Cultural Inventory. Through participatory
methods, the community will identify and document local attractions, unique traditions, and tourism assets that can be further developed and promoted. 
5. Activity 5: Digital Marketing and Promotion. The team will assist the
community in creating basic promotional materials such as brochures, social media
content, and short videos to showcase their destination and attract visitors. 
6. Activity 6: Stakeholder Consultations and Action Planning. The final phase
includes a community consultation where participants will create an initial tourism
development action plan to ensure continuity and sustainability beyond the duration of the project. Each activity will be facilitated by experts from the academe and tourism sector, ensuring that content is both practical and grounded in current industry standards. The project also encourages collaboration between the university and the community, fostering mutual growth and empowerment.

column4: Advancing Siargao’s Economic Competitiveness Through Technology-Enabled Language Solutions
column6:
This program is a multi-component applied research and innovation initiative that addresses language barriers as a critical factor affecting tourism experience, MSME visibility, and inclusive economic participation in Siargao Island. As a global tourism destination, Siargao faces growing demand for effective multilingual communication among tourism workers, enterprises, and visitors.

The project integrates digital learning tools, language-driven marketing solutions, and mobile translation technologies to enhance service quality and enterprise competitiveness. Instructional English video modules will equip tourism frontliners with practical communication skills. Language-focused promotional materials will help micro and small enterprises present their products more effectively to local and international markets. A multilingual mobile translation application will facilitate real-time communication across Surigaonon, Tagalog, and English.

By combining technology, language, and culture, the program supports tourism-led economic growth, MSME development, cultural preservation, and inclusive participation, contributing to a more competitive and visitor-friendly Siargao economy.

column4: Construction of Three-Storey Maritime Resource Center
column6: The construction of a new three-storey Maritime Resource Center Building will provide dedicated office space for NMP’s digital resource center, designed to enhance the agency’s capability to deliver timely, accurate, and accessible maritime data to government agencies, industry stakeholders, and seafarers. The digital resource center will facilitate streamlined information-sharing and ensure that Filipino seafarers have access to up-to-date information on employment regulations, training opportunities, and helpline support for their welfare and career advancement. In addition, the Maritime Resource Center will strengthen policy formulation and program implementation by providing reliable data analytics to effectively address industry challenges and workforce demands.
